blocks.title: Actors and Responsibilities
blocks.content:
### Actors and Responsibilities

VHL defines four core actors that participate in the issuance and redemption of a Verifiable Health Link:

| Actor | ActorDefinition Canonical | Role in VHL |
|---|---|---|
| **VHL Holder** | `https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/VHL/ActorDefinition/VHLHolder` | Individual (or personal health wallet application acting on the individual's behalf) that requests generation of a VHL from a VHL Sharer (`[ITI-YY3]`) and presents the VHL to a VHL Receiver (`[ITI-YY4]`). |
| **VHL Sharer** | `https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/VHL/ActorDefinition/VHLSharer` | System that publishes i

summary.text: Defines VHL's four actors with their ActorDefinition canonicals: the VHL Holder (an individual or their personal health wallet) requests a VHL from a Sharer and presents it to a Receiver; the VHL Sharer publishes its signing material to a Trust Anchor, generates signed VHL payloads and serves the manifest and documents; the VHL Receiver verifies the VHL against the Trust Anchor's trust list and retrieves the manifest and documents; the Trust Anchor accepts participants' public keys and distributes signed trust lists such as DID documents or X.509/JWKS lists.

blocks.title: Trust-Anchor Neutrality
blocks.content:
### Trust-Anchor Neutrality

IHE VHL is **trust-anchor neutral** by design. The **Trust Anchor** actor represents any trust framework authority capable of accepting PKI material (`[ITI-YY1]`) and distributing verifiable trust lists (`[ITI-YY2]`). The **WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN)** is one possible Trust Anchor implementation among others (such as national health PKI roots, regional cross-border trust networks, or bilateral federation anchors). No VHL transaction hardcodes a single trust network host; participants resolve issuer and receiver keys through the configur

summary.text: States that VHL is trust-anchor neutral by design: the Trust Anchor actor stands for any trust framework authority that accepts PKI material and distributes trust lists, the WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network (GDHCN) being one possible implementation among others such as national PKI roots, regional cross-border networks or bilateral federation anchors. No transaction hardcodes a trust network host; keys are resolved through the configured Trust Anchor's [ITI-YY2] trust list.

blocks.title: Composite Grouping with IHE PCF (Privacy Consent on FHIR)
blocks.content:
### Composite Grouping with IHE PCF (Privacy Consent on FHIR)

When a **VHL Sharer** is grouped with IHE PCF actors (**Consent Recorder**, **Consent Registry**, and/or **Consent Authorization Server**):

1. Before or during VHL issuance (`[ITI-YY3]`), the VHL Holder records or selects a patient privacy consent directive stored via **PCF Access Consent `[ITI-108]`**, scoping which documents, purposes of use, recipients, or validity periods the VHL covers.
2. When a **VHL Receiver** redeems the VHL via **Retrieve Manifest `[ITI-YY5]`**, the **VHL Sharer** evaluates the active PCF `Consent` direc

summary.text: Describes grouping a VHL Sharer with IHE PCF actors: before or during issuance the Holder records or selects a consent directive via PCF [ITI-108] that scopes the documents, purposes, recipients or validity period the VHL covers, and when a Receiver redeems the VHL through Retrieve Manifest [ITI-YY5] the Sharer evaluates the active Consent directives against the requester, purpose, documents and time before returning anything.

blocks.title: Summary of VHL Transactions
blocks.content:
### Summary of VHL Transactions

| Transaction Code | Transaction Name | Initiator | Responder | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **`[ITI-YY1]`** | **Submit PKI Material with DID** | VHL Sharer / VHL Receiver | Trust Anchor | Submits public key material (DID document / JWK Set / X.509 certificate metadata) to the Trust Anchor for inclusion in the trust network's published key list. |
| **`[ITI-YY2]`** | **Retrieve Trust List with DID** | VHL Receiver / VHL Sharer | Trust Anchor | Retrieves the signed trust list (DID document / JWK Set) from the Trust Anchor to verify signatures on VHL pay

summary.text: Tabulates the five VHL transactions with initiator and responder: [ITI-YY1] Submit PKI Material with DID (Sharer or Receiver to Trust Anchor); [ITI-YY2] Retrieve Trust List with DID, used to verify VHL signatures and mutual TLS; [ITI-YY3] Generate VHL (Holder to Sharer, via $generate-vhl, optionally bound to a PCF Consent and selective-disclosure parameters, returning a signed payload such as HCERT, CWT or a SMART Health Link URI); [ITI-YY4] Provide VHL (Holder to Receiver by QR code, deep link or near-field exchange); and [ITI-YY5] Retrieve Manifest (Receiver to Sharer, returning a Bundle of DocumentReference entries).

blocks.title: OperationDefinition: Generate VHL (`$generate-vhl`, `[ITI-YY3]`)
blocks.content:
### OperationDefinition: Generate VHL (`$generate-vhl`, `[ITI-YY3]`)

The `GenerateVHL` operation (`https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/VHL/OperationDefinition/GenerateVHL`, code `generate-vhl`) is invoked on a **VHL Sharer** at the system level (`POST [base]/$generate-vhl`). It accepts subject identification, optional document selection or folder references, expiration / passcode parameters, and consent directive references, and returns the signed VHL payload for storage on the VHL Holder's Personal Health Wallet.

summary.text: Describes the GenerateVHL operation ($generate-vhl, [ITI-YY3]), invoked at system level on a VHL Sharer with POST [base]/$generate-vhl: it takes subject identification, optional document or folder selection, expiry and passcode parameters and consent directive references, and returns the signed VHL payload to be stored in the Holder's Personal Health Wallet.
